newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva airport says 1996 profits, passengers dip.
newsitem.headline: Geneva airport says 1996 profits, passengers dip.

text.p: Geneva's Cointrin international airport, hit by national carrier Swissair's decision to switch most long-haul flights to Zurich, on Thursday reported a sharp drop in profits, passengers and cargo in 1996.

But Board President Jean-Philippe Maitre told a news conference the airport, which serves a wide region of western Switzerland and Alpine France, was not in danger and its financial director said it had reached "cruising speed".
Net profits dropped from 8.9 million Swiss francs to 3.6 million Swiss francs, Maitre said, but this was partly because improvement costs originally set for 1995 were delayed into last year.

Airport Director-General Jean-Pierre Jobin said passengers passing through Cointrin totalled 6.18 million, a 1.4 percent drop on 1995 -- which had been the airport's best year ever with a total of 6.22 million.
Jobin blamed the decline largely on Swissair's controversial move, which affected flights to Asia, the Middle East and North America and went into effect at the end of October last year.
Until October, departing passenger numbers had been increasing at a rate of one percent a month. But in November and again in December they declined by five percent, he said.
At the same time, he indicated, passenger totals in 1995 had been inflated by the big international telecommunications exhibition Telecom, which is held in geneva every four years.

He said transit passengers had also declined by over 17 percent because of the cancellation of the inter-continental routes while many Swiss-based travellers who now preferred to go to Zurich by car or train to pick up long-haul flights.
Jobin reported that cargo moved through the airport, which had hit an all-time high of 68,914 tonnes in 1995, dropped back by 7.3 percent to 63,871 in 1996.
